title: The Fighting Cricket
synopsis: A tale of the hardships facing a man trying to find a fierce cricket for the emperor!

fullText.simplified:
一千多年前，有个皇帝，他很喜欢玩斗蛐蛐。
    斗蛐蛐，就是把两只蛐蛐放在一个盘子里，让它们打架，看哪只蛐蛐能赢。
    皇帝喜欢玩斗蛐蛐，大家就得去找蛐蛐。很多地方的市长都从自己的地方找来厉害的蛐蛐，送去给皇帝。找到厉害蛐蛐的人，会把蛐蛐卖得很贵。很多人把房子卖了，把家里所有的东西都卖了，都不一定买得起一只蛐蛐。
    有一个地方，叫花阴市。这个地方没有蛐蛐，但是这个花阴市的市长想让皇帝喜欢他，就花了很多钱，从别的地方买了一只很厉害的蛐蛐送去给皇帝。没想到，这只蛐蛐真的很厉害，一下子打败了很多蛐蛐。皇帝很高兴，就让这个市长每年都送一只蛐蛐来。
    市长不可能每年都花那么多钱去买蛐蛐，怎么办？皇帝要市长交蛐蛐，市长可以要村长交蛐蛐。因为皇帝下面有很多市长，市长下面有很多村长。所以，这个市长就让每个村的村长每年秋天交一只蛐蛐上来。交上来的蛐蛐市长会让它们斗，最厉害的那只就会送去给皇帝。
    村里面一些没有工作的人每天都会去找蛐蛐。找到好蛐蛐，他们就会把它放进一个金色的笼子里，拿去卖，卖得非常贵。村长要么去和这些人买蛐蛐，要么自己去捉蛐蛐。钱没有，蛐蛐也不好找。交不上蛐蛐，就要被打，所以谁也不想当村长。
fullText.traditional:
一千多年前，有個皇帝，他很喜歡玩鬥蛐蛐。
    鬥蛐蛐，就是把兩隻蛐蛐放在一個盤子裡，讓它們打架，看哪隻蛐蛐能贏。
    皇帝喜歡玩鬥蛐蛐，大家就得去找蛐蛐。很多地方的市長都從自己的地方找來厲害的蛐蛐，送去給皇帝。找到厲害蛐蛐的人，會把蛐蛐賣得很貴。很多人把房子賣了，把家裡所有的東西都賣了，都不一定買得起一隻蛐蛐。
    有一個地方，叫花陰市。這個地方沒有蛐蛐，但是這個花陰市的市長想讓皇帝喜歡他，就花了很多錢，從別的地方買了一隻很厲害的蛐蛐送去給皇帝。沒想到，這隻蛐蛐真的很厲害，一下子打敗了很多蛐蛐。皇帝很高興，就讓這個市長每年都送一隻蛐蛐來。
    市長不可能每年都花那麼多錢去買蛐蛐，怎麼辦？皇帝要市長交蛐蛐，市長可以要村長交蛐蛐。因為皇帝下面有很多市長，市長下面有很多村長。所以，這個市長就讓每個村的村長每年秋天交一隻蛐蛐上來。交上來的蛐蛐市長會讓它們鬥，最厲害的那隻就會送去給皇帝。
    村裡面一些沒有工作的人每天都會去找蛐蛐。找到好蛐蛐，他們就會把它放進一個金色的籠子裡，拿去賣，賣得非常貴。村長要麼去和這些人買蛐蛐，要麼自己去捉蛐蛐。錢沒有，蛐蛐也不好找。交不上蛐蛐，就要被打，所以誰也不想當村長。

sentences.simplified: 一千多年前，有个皇帝，他很喜欢玩斗蛐蛐。
sentences.traditional: 一千多年前，有個皇帝，他很喜歡玩鬥蛐蛐。
sentences.pinyin: yì qiān duō nián qián yǒu ge huáng dì tā hěn xǐ huan wán dòu qū qū
sentences.english: More than a thousand years ago, there was an emperor who enjoyed cricket fighting.

sentences.simplified: 斗蛐蛐，就是把两只蛐蛐放在一个盘子里，
sentences.traditional: 鬥蛐蛐，就是把兩隻蛐蛐放在一個盤子裡，
sentences.pinyin: dòu qū qū jiù shì bǎ liǎng zhī qū qū fàng zài yí ge pán zi lǐ
sentences.english: To fight crickets, you just take two crickets and put them in a tray, ..

sentences.simplified: 让它们打架，看哪只蛐蛐能赢。
sentences.traditional: 讓它們打架，看哪隻蛐蛐能贏。
sentences.pinyin: ràng tā men dǎ jià kàn nǎ zhī qū qū néng yíng
sentences.english: .. to make them fight each other and see which cricket wins.

sentences.simplified: 皇帝喜欢玩斗蛐蛐，大家就得去找蛐蛐。
sentences.traditional: 皇帝喜歡玩鬥蛐蛐，大家就得去找蛐蛐。
sentences.pinyin: huáng dì xǐ huan wán dòu qū qū dà jiā jiù děi qù zhǎo qū qū
sentences.english: The emperor enjoyed cricket fighting, so everyone had to look for crickets.

sentences.simplified: 很多地方的市长都从自己的地方找来厉害的蛐蛐，送去给皇帝。
sentences.traditional: 很多地方的市長都從自己的地方找來厲害的蛐蛐，送去給皇帝。
sentences.pinyin: hěn duō dì fang de shì zhǎng dōu cóng zì jǐ de dì fang zhǎo lái lì hai de qū qū sòng qù gěi huáng dì
sentences.english: Many mayors would look for fierce crickets from their area to send to the emperor.

sentences.simplified: 找到厉害蛐蛐的人，会把蛐蛐卖得很贵。
sentences.traditional: 找到厲害蛐蛐的人，會把蛐蛐賣得很貴。
sentences.pinyin: zhǎo dào lì hai qū qū de rén huì bǎ qū qū mài de hěn guì
sentences.english: The people who found fierce crickets would sell them at very high prices.

sentences.simplified: 很多人把房子卖了，把家里所有的东西都卖了，都不一定买得起一只蛐蛐。
sentences.traditional: 很多人把房子賣了，把家裡所有的東西都賣了，都不一定買得起一隻蛐蛐。
sentences.pinyin: hěn duō rén bǎ fáng zi mài le bǎ jiā lǐ suǒ yǒu de dōng xi dōu mài le dōu bù yí dìng mǎi de qǐ yì zhī qū qū
sentences.english: A lot of people couldn’t afford to buy a cricket even if they sold their house and everything in it.

sentences.simplified: 有一个地方，叫花阴市。
sentences.traditional: 有一個地方，叫花陰市。
sentences.pinyin: yǒu yí ge dì fang jiào huā yīn shì
sentences.english: There was a place called Huayin City.

sentences.simplified: 这个地方没有蛐蛐，但是这个花阴市的市长想让皇帝喜欢他，
sentences.traditional: 這個地方沒有蛐蛐，但是這個花陰市的市長想讓皇帝喜歡他，
sentences.pinyin: zhè ge dì fang méi yǒu qū qū dàn shì zhè ge huā yīn shì de shì zhǎng xiǎng ràng huáng dì xǐ huan tā
sentences.english: This place didn’t have crickets, but the mayor of Huayin City wanted to make the emperor like him.

sentences.simplified: 就花了很多钱，从别的地方买了一只很厉害的蛐蛐送去给皇帝。
sentences.traditional: 就花了很多錢，從別的地方買了一隻很厲害的蛐蛐送去給皇帝。
sentences.pinyin: jiù huā le hěn duō qián cóng bié de dì fang mǎi le yì zhī hěn lì hai de qū qū sòng qù gěi huáng dì
sentences.english: So he spent a lot of money to buy a fierce cricket from somewhere else and give it to the emperor.

sentences.simplified: 没想到，这只蛐蛐真的很厉害，一下子打败了很多蛐蛐。
sentences.traditional: 沒想到，這隻蛐蛐真的很厲害，一下子打敗了很多蛐蛐。
sentences.pinyin: méi xiǎng dào zhè zhī qū qū zhēn de hěn lì hai yí xià zi dǎ bài le hěn duō qū qū
sentences.english: Unexpectedly, this cricket really was very fierce, and defeated many other crickets in a short period.

sentences.simplified: 皇帝很高兴，就让这个市长每年都送一只蛐蛐来。
sentences.traditional: 皇帝很高興，就讓這個市長每年都送一隻蛐蛐來。
sentences.pinyin: huáng dì hěn gāo xìng jiù ràng zhè ge shì zhǎng měi nián dōu sòng yì zhī qū qū lái
sentences.english: The emperor was very happy, and requested this mayor to send a cricket every year.

sentences.simplified: 市长不可能每年都花那么多钱去买蛐蛐，怎么办？
sentences.traditional: 市長不可能每年都花那麼多錢去買蛐蛐，怎麼辦？
sentences.pinyin: shì zhǎng bù kě néng měi nián dōu huā nà me duō qián qù mǎi qū qū zěn me bàn
sentences.english: It wasn’t possible for the mayor to spend that much money to buy a cricket every year, so what to do?

sentences.simplified: 皇帝要市长交蛐蛐，市长可以要村长交蛐蛐。
sentences.traditional: 皇帝要市長交蛐蛐，市長可以要村長交蛐蛐。
sentences.pinyin: huáng dì yào shì zhǎng jiāo qū qū shì zhǎng kě yǐ yào cūn zhǎng jiāo qū qū
sentences.english: The emperor asked the mayor to hand over crickets, and the mayor could ask village chiefs to hand over crickets.

sentences.simplified: 因为皇帝下面有很多市长，市长下面有很多村长。
sentences.traditional: 因為皇帝下面有很多市長，市長下面有很多村長。
sentences.pinyin: yīn wèi huáng dì xià miàn yǒu hěn duō shì zhǎng shì zhǎng xià miàn yǒu hěn duō cūn zhǎng
sentences.english: Because there were a lot of mayors under the emperor, there were a lot of village chiefs under the mayor.

sentences.simplified: 所以，这个市长就让每个村的村长每年秋天交一只蛐蛐上来。
sentences.traditional: 所以，這個市長就讓每個村的村長每年秋天交一隻蛐蛐上來。
sentences.pinyin: suǒ yǐ zhè ge shì zhǎng jiù ràng měi ge cūn de cūn zhǎng měi nián qiū tiān jiāo yì zhī qū qū shàng lái
sentences.english: So every autumn, this mayor made the chief of every village hand over a cricket.

sentences.simplified: 交上来的蛐蛐市长会让它们斗，
sentences.traditional: 交上來的蛐蛐市長會讓它們鬥，
sentences.pinyin: jiāo shàng lái de qū qū shì zhǎng huì ràng tā men dòu
sentences.english: The crickets that the village chiefs handed over would be made to fight by the mayor, ..

sentences.simplified: 最厉害的那只就会送去给皇帝。
sentences.traditional: 最厲害的那隻就會送去給皇帝。
sentences.pinyin: zuì lì hai de nà zhī jiù huì sòng qù gěi huáng dì
sentences.english: .. and the fiercest one would be given to the emperor.

sentences.simplified: 村里面一些没有工作的人每天都会去找蛐蛐。
sentences.traditional: 村裡面一些沒有工作的人每天都會去找蛐蛐。
sentences.pinyin: cūn lǐ miàn yì xiē méi yǒu gōng zuò de rén měi tiān dōu huì qù zhǎo qū qū
sentences.english: Some people in the villages that didn’t have work would go look for crickets every day.

sentences.simplified: 找到好蛐蛐，他们就会把它放进一个金色的笼子里，拿去卖，卖得非常贵。
sentences.traditional: 找到好蛐蛐，他們就會把它放進一個金色的籠子裡，拿去賣，賣得非常貴。
sentences.pinyin: zhǎo dào hǎo qū qū tā men jiù huì bǎ tā fàng jìn yí ge jīn sè de lóng zi lǐ ná qù mài mài de fēi cháng guì
sentences.english: When they found a good cricket, they would put it in a golden cage and sell it for an extremely high price.

sentences.simplified: 村长要么去和这些人买蛐蛐，要么自己去捉蛐蛐。
sentences.traditional: 村長要麼去和這些人買蛐蛐，要麼自己去捉蛐蛐。
sentences.pinyin: cūn zhǎng yào me qù hé zhè xiē rén mǎi qū qū yào me zì jǐ qù zhuō qū qū
sentences.english: The village chiefs would either buy crickets from these people, or go catch crickets themselves.

sentences.simplified: 钱没有，蛐蛐也不好找。
sentences.traditional: 錢沒有，蛐蛐也不好找。
sentences.pinyin: qián méi yǒu qū qū yě bù hǎo zhǎo
sentences.english: Without money, crickets were not easy to find.

sentences.simplified: 交不上蛐蛐，就要被打，所以谁也不想当村长。
sentences.traditional: 交不上蛐蛐，就要被打，所以誰也不想當村長。
sentences.pinyin: jiāo bú shàng qū qū jiù yào bèi dǎ suǒ yǐ shéi yě bù xiǎng dāng cūn zhǎng
sentences.english: Not handing over a cricket meant that you would be beaten, so no one wanted to be a village chief.

sentence_translations: More than a thousand years ago, there was an emperor who enjoyed cricket fighting.
To fight crickets, you just take two crickets and put them in a tray, ..
.. to make them fight each other and see which cricket wins.
The emperor enjoyed cricket fighting, so everyone had to look for crickets.
Many mayors would look for fierce crickets from their area to send to the emperor.
The people who found fierce crickets would sell them at very high prices.
A lot of people couldn’t afford to buy a cricket even if they sold their house and everything in it.
There was a place called Huayin City.
This place didn’t have crickets, but the mayor of Huayin City wanted to make the emperor like him.
So he spent a lot of money to buy a fierce cricket from somewhere else and give it to the emperor.
Unexpectedly, this cricket really was very fierce, and defeated many other crickets in a short period.
The emperor was very happy, and requested this mayor to send a cricket every year.
It wasn’t possible for the mayor to spend that much money to buy a cricket every year, so what to do?
The emperor asked the mayor to hand over crickets, and the mayor could ask village chiefs to hand over crickets.
Because there were a lot of mayors under the emperor, there were a lot of village chiefs under the mayor.
So every autumn, this mayor made the chief of every village hand over a cricket.
The crickets that the village chiefs handed over would be made to fight by the mayor, ..
.. and the fiercest one would be given to the emperor.
Some people in the villages that didn’t have work would go look for crickets every day.
When they found a good cricket, they would put it in a golden cage and sell it for an extremely high price.
The village chiefs would either buy crickets from these people, or go catch crickets themselves.
Without money, crickets were not easy to find.
Not handing over a cricket meant that you would be beaten, so no one wanted to be a village chief.
